title: Define packet defaults and elide repeated attributes

state.decision_rationale: Accepted selectively: default projection, reason, and false export are elided; local trust=data and explicit depth remain.

provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Define packet-level defaults and only annotate deviations instead of repeating projection=exact reason=selected, trust=data, exported=true, and depth where parent chains already encode it.
feedback.normalized_claim: Move common values into explicit scoped defaults and omit redundant record attributes when their values remain unambiguous and mechanically reconstructable.

current_behavior: Every file index row emits projection and reason, every exact content and chunk header repeats trust=data, and every symbol emits depth and exported.
Repeated local trust markers were an intentional response to long-context instruction-boundary decay.
Depth is derivable from parent links only when the full, valid parent chain is present; exported meaning is analyzer- and language-dependent.
The format has no normative default declaration or inheritance rules.

proposal.summary: Evaluate explicit, scoped defaults for high-frequency attributes while preserving local trust reinforcement and simple streaming interpretation where those benefits outweigh token savings.
candidate_changes: Define defaults at packet or block scope for projection, selection reason, trust, and other genuinely uniform fields.
Specify inheritance, override, reset, and unknown-default behavior for streaming consumers.
Compare retaining trust=data locally against stronger guide wording and chunk byte framing.
Elide derivable depth or exported fields only where semantics and validation remain clear.
non_goals: Do not remove local source-as-data signals solely for byte savings without model-safety evaluation.
Do not make records depend on hidden implementation defaults.
Do not treat exported=true on config structures as meaningful without defining analyzer semantics.

questions: Which repeated fields dominate tokenizer cost rather than raw bytes?
Does local trust repetition measurably reduce instruction confusion in long packets?
Can a consumer validate depth more cheaply when it is explicit than when derived?
risks: Inherited defaults increase parser state and make isolated records less self-contained.
Removing trust markers may weaken model-facing boundaries despite equivalent parser semantics.
Default changes across versions can silently reinterpret omitted fields.
evidence_needed: Token-frequency and compressed-size analysis by attribute.
Prompt-injection evaluations with local versus inherited trust declarations.
Parser complexity and isolated-record usability comparisons.
